To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a series of six-coordinated copper(ii) complexes have been synthesized and characterized by X-ray diffraction and other spectroscopic techniques.
bis(3, 5-di-t-butlyprazol-1- yl)acetate-anchored copper(ii) complexes with cis-aquo ligand(s) are promising catalysts for oxidation of catechols to quinones.

a series of six-coordinated copper(ii) complexes with the bis(pyrazol)acetate ligand and N-heteroatom bases or aliphatic chelating ligands have been prepared and characterized, and the cis-aqua copper complex demonstrates higher activity in performing the catalytic oxidation of 3-tert-butlycatechol to 3,tert-butyl-quinone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new copper catalysts for catalyzing the aerobic oxidation of 3-5-DTBC to 3, 5-DTBQ.
the synthesis and structure of bis(pyrazole-1-yl)-acetate-embedded Cu(II) complexes, and the catalytic oxidation of 3.5-DTBC to 3, 5-DTBQ by the complexes.
the synthesis and characterization of a series of copper(ii) complexes with a bis(pyrazolato)acetato ligand and other nitrogen donors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bis(pyrazolato)acetate-bridged copper(ii) complexes are capable of catalyzing the oxidation of 3-5-di-tertbutoxyphenol to 3, 5-di-ter-butylquinone in a manner that is similar to the catechol oxidase.
a combination of bis(pyrazoyl)acetate and cis-aqua ligands is essential to the catalytic oxidation of 3.5-DTBC to 3.5-TBQ.
the catalytic activity of the copper complexes is strongly dependent on the coordination mode and the steric hindrance of the bis(pyrazol)acetate ligand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the steric hindrance of the bis(pyrazol)acetate ligand can be used to tune the coordination geometry of the copper(ii) center to achieve a higher catalytic efficiency.
the catecholase activities of the copper complexes are closely associated with the coordination geometry of the metal centers.
the catecholase activities of copper(ii) complexes are not only determined by the electronic properties of the ligands, but also the steric and structural features of the complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bis(pyrazol)acetate ligand is not only an efficient ligand for copper complexes to perform catalytic oxidation, but also an ideal ligand for tuning the catalytic activity through ligand modification.
the steric bulkiness and coordination mode of bdtbpza are important for tuning the catalytic performance of copper(ii) complexes.
the bis(pyrazoloyl)acetate ligand is an excellent anchor that can be used in the construction of new metal complexes for catalytic applications.
